source.title: Understanding and Enhancing the Transferability of Jailbreaking Attacks
source.authors: Runqi Lin; Bo Han; Fengwang Li; Tong Liu

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether adversarial suffix and prompt attacks bypass safety using harmful-response rates, but uses attack interventions and evaluation measures different from the original fine-tuning and token-position-KL methods.
record.gate_note: Tests harmful-response rates for GCG suffixes and PAIR prompts, which bear on V4. PiF changes tokens in the input but is not a compliant-opening prefill, suffix, or decoding change; its attack-rate results are recorded under none and described in fits_no_version. The paper also reports perceived-importance results, which are not per-response-position KL measurements. AHS values are not separate rows because they assess harmfulness rather than refusal/compliance rates. Results attributed to other papers are not included.
record.test_reason: Table 2 and Table 12 report how often GCG adversarial suffixes, built on Llama-2-7B-Chat, get six aligned target models past refusal. These are baselines in a paper on a new attack (PiF), but they are still measured rates of suffixes defeating refusal. Only the GCG suffix rows bear on V4. PAIR rewrites the whole prompt and PiF swaps tokens, so neither is a prefill, suffix or decoding change. No fine-tuning, per-position KL, parameter localization or deepening is studied.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that jailbreaks divert the source model's focus from malicious-intent tokens. They also conclude that lengthy adversarial sequences overfit the source model (distributional dependency), so transfer is unreliable. PiF, which flattens perceived importance via synonym replacement, is presented as transferring with high ASR to proprietary models including GPT-4 and o1.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates prompt- and token-level jailbreak attacks and PiF token replacement, not fine-tuning or response-position KL. It uses ASR and harmfulness ratings, with perceived-importance analyses.
record.method_sensitivity: GCG effectiveness varies substantially by target model and dataset; Table 4 shows substantial effects of defence method. The paper also reports different ASRs under optimal attack configurations in Table 12.

fits_no_version.finding: PiF synonym-replacement prompts reach 82–100% refusal-substring ASR across targets, including GPT-4 and o1. The published PiF examples end the input with 'assistant: sure, here is'.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Token-replacement prompts that disperse attention away from malicious-intent tokens transfer across models and bypass refusal.

fits_no_version.finding: PAIR prompt-rewriting attacks transfer with 51–91% ASR, but with low harmfulness scores (AHS 1.3–2.4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Prompt-level rewriting jailbreaks transfer more stably than suffixes across aligned models.

fits_no_version.finding: Under a 'This intent is [MASK]' probe, aligned models concentrate importance on malicious-intent tokens (e.g. 'bomb' 37%), and jailbreaks divert it (Figures 2–3). This concerns input tokens, not response positions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety refusal depends on intent recognition over input tokens.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the ASR values. The paper notes that a comprehensive theoretical analysis of transfer mechanisms remains open and that attacks can still produce safety disclaimers at the end of responses. The reported GCG rates vary markedly by target and dataset.
record.rows_left_out: The one-query warm-up results in Table 14 were not extracted. AHS values were not given separate rows because they measure output harmfulness rather than the refusal/compliance rate named in V4. The perceived-importance comparisons and Table 5 variation values were not extracted as rows because they do not measure response-position KL or the V4 behaviour. Other-method comparison values attributed to original papers were excluded.

untested.parts: Per-position KL between aligned and base models.
Compliant-opening prefill and decoding changes. GCG on its own source model (white-box) is not reported; only transfer to other models is.
Localization of safety in weights or ranks.
Causes of shallowness in data or objective.

missing.what: AHS (harmfulness score, 1–5) for GCG suffixes: about 1.05 on the Llama targets, 2.48–3.68 on Vicuna/Mistral, 1.53–2.27 on GPT models. This shows whether bypassed refusals actually yield harmful content.

record.verdict_notes: GCG and PAIR are baselines for the paper's own attack, and ASR is refusal-substring matching. Only transferred GCG (built on Llama-2-7B-Chat) bears on V4, and only in a transfer setting. Its failure on Llama targets reflects transfer, not a failure of suffixes on the model they were built for. The record's 'limits_scope' label for defences was dropped because GCG was already near 0% on Llama-2-13B before any defence. PiF inputs include a 'sure, here is' cue that resembles a prefill, but the paper does not isolate its effect.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful fine-tuning and refusal after fine-tuning.
Benign fine-tuning and refusal after fine-tuning.
Per-token KL divergence across aligned and base model response positions.
Compliant-opening prefill and decoding changes are not tested as interventions; attack outcomes are reported for suffix/prompt methods, not as a general test of every way of getting past an opening.
Localization of safety behaviour in weights or ranks.
Whether safety-training data or objective causes shallow safety.
Training to deepen safety and whether that training holds up.

relationships.condition: Transferred GCG suffixes on Vicuna-13B and Mistral-7B (both datasets), and on GPT-4-0613 and GPT-o1-preview on MaliciousInstruct
relationships.reason: Refusal-substring ASR is 72–96 (r13, r16, r19, r22, r28, r34).
relationships.display_finding: Measured by refusal-substring matching, ASR was 72–96% on Vicuna-13B, Mistral-7B, GPT-4-0613 and GPT-o1-preview.

relationships.condition: Transferred GCG suffixes on Llama-2-13B-Chat and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
relationships.reason: ASR is 1.4–3.0 (r01, r04, r07, r10) and only 32.1 under GCG's optimal settings (r53). Transferred suffixes largely fail to defeat refusal on these targets.
relationships.display_finding: Transferred suffixes reach only 1.4–3.0 ASR on these targets, and 32.1 even under GCG's optimal settings.

relationships.condition: Transferred GCG suffixes on GPT-4-0613 and GPT-o1-preview, AdvBench
relationships.reason: ASR is only 27.2–46.9 (r25, r31, r56), against 72–87 on MaliciousInstruct, so success depends on dataset.
relationships.display_finding: ASR on AdvBench is only 27.2–46.9, against 72–87 on MaliciousInstruct, so success depends on the dataset.
